candidate.answerReason: Redistributing the coins shows that five chests held nine coins each. There were seven chests in total, and 45=6·7+3, so both original conditions hold.

methods.label: Move coins between the arrangements
methods.explanation:
Start with the arrangement having \(6\) coins in every chest and \(3\) coins left over. To reach the arrangement with two empty chests, empty two of these chests. This releases \(2\cdot6=12\) coins.

Together with the \(3\) leftover coins, there are now \(15\) coins available to increase the contents of the remaining chests from \(6\) to \(9\). Each remaining chest needs \(9-6=3\) more coins, so there must be
\[
15\div3=5
\]
remaining chests. All the coins are in those five chests in the nine-coin arrangement, giving
\[
5\cdot9=45
\]
gold coins.

There are \(5+2=7\) chests altogether, and \(6\cdot7+3=45\), which also satisfies the six-coin condition. The answer is \(45\), choice \(\text{C}\).
